key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over minutes to hours. LOCATION: UNILATERAL or bilateral. DURATION: Lasts 4-72 hours. CHARACTER: THROBBING, PULSATING pain. AGGRAVATING: LIGHT, sound, movement, stress. RELIEVING: DARK, quiet room, sleep, medications. TIMING: Gradual onset, lasts 4-72 hours. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: NAUSEA, vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia, may have aura (visual, sensory, motor). KEY POSITIVES: Throbbing pain, nausea, photophobia, phonophobia, aura. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Sudden severe headache - possible subarachnoid hemorrhage, call 911
Headache with neck stiffness and fever - possible meningitis, call 911
Headache with focal neurological deficits - possible stroke, call 911
Headache with signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Headache with severe hypertension - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
